name: Cessna 190/195
summary: Cessna's only postwar radial-engine airplane: a large, all-metal 4–5 seat tailwheel 'Businessliner' with a cantilever wing and a big round cowling.

wings: Cantilever high wing with no struts
engines: Single air-cooled radial in a large, round cowling
fuselage: Deep, wide cabin with a door each side and a large rear window
Fixed spring-steel main gear with a tailwheel

tellTales: Radial engine in front of a high wing with no struts
Large round cowling and deep cabin on a tailwheel
Tall, swept tail and flat spring-steel gear

confusedWith.howToTell: The 195 has a radial engine and a bigger round cowl with no wing struts; the 180 has a slim flat engine and a strut-braced wing.
The 195 has a radial engine in a large round cowl; the 170 has a flat engine in a slim nose.
The 195 is a single with a high wing; the Beech 18 is a twin with a low wing.
The 195 has a radial engine, no struts and a tailwheel; the 182 has a flat engine, a lift strut and (mostly) a nosewheel.
